acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Host Ira Glass goes to a block in New York City where, over a year into the pandemic, neighbors are still clapping for health care workers every night at 7 p.m.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: Producer Ben Calhoun investigates a daily mystery—a daily musical mystery.
acts.title: How Do You Get To Carnegie Hall?

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Dee Brown’s routine is thrown totally out of whack when Covid hits. Her granddaughter, Cecilia Brown, helps her come up with a new one, and along the way documents a thing she never expected to.
acts.title: So Nice to Hear Your Voice

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: For the last five years or so, Johnny Dark has kept up a very specific, unusual, and labor intensive daily practice. Kelefa Sanneh talks to him about it.
acts.title: It Had to Be YouTube

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Host Ira Glass with the last piece in today’s show, inspired by the New York Times podcast, The Daily.
acts.title: Here’s What Else You Need To Know Today
